clue: The circular target area at each end of the sheet consisting of four concentric rings.
note: Scoring is determined solely by stones that touch or rest inside the twelve-foot outer circle of the house.

clue: The tactical advantage of throwing the final stone in an end.
note: The team without last-stone advantage in the first end earns it if the other team scores points.

clue: A shot delivered with precise weight to come to rest inside the house without striking another stone.
note: Mastering draw weight is widely considered the foundational skill of elite curling delivery.

clue: The smooth Teflon or stainless steel sole worn on a curler's sliding foot to facilitate a long delivery glide.
note: Sliders vary in thickness, with thicker Teflon providing higher speed and less friction on the ice.

clue: Tiny frozen water droplets sprayed onto the ice sheet before play to reduce surface friction.
note: Without pebble, the flat running band of the stone would create immense suction against the smooth ice and stop quickly.

clue: The uninhabited Scottish island that is the primary historical quarry for curling stone granite.
note: Common Green and Blue Hone granites harvested from Ailsa Craig are prized for low water absorption and impact resistance.

clue: The rule prohibiting teams from eliminating an opponent's stone positioned between the tee line and hog line outside the house before the sixth stone.
note: The modernization from a four-stone to a five-stone Free Guard Zone in 2018 dramatically increased offensive play.

clue: The team captain who directs strategy from the house and traditionally throws the final two stones.
note: While the skip traditionally throws fourth, team rules permit any player to hold skip duties regardless of throwing order.

clue: The centuries-old Scottish nickname for curling inspired by the sound of stones traveling over pebbled ice.
note: Curling's earliest physical evidence includes stones inscribed with dates as early as 1511 in Stirling, Scotland.

clue: Modern sweeping technique where a brush head angle and motion influence a stone's curl path and lateral direction.
note: Revolutions in broom fabric and directional sweeping led World Curling to standardize brush head fabrics in 2016.

clue: A delicate draw shot that comes to rest touching or barely nestled against an opponent's stone.
note: An executed freeze makes it almost impossible for the opponent to remove the delivered stone without also displacing their own.

clue: The French host venue where men's curling made its official Olympic debut retroactively confirmed by the IOC in 2006.
note: Great Britain won the gold medal in 1924, skipped by Willie Jackson on outdoor natural ice sheets.

clue: The prestigious annual Canadian men's curling championship first contested at Toronto's Granite Club in 1927.
note: Winners of the Brier receive the iconic purple heart crests and the right to represent Canada at the World Championship.

clue: An optional tactical setting once per game allowing a team with hammer to place pre-positioned stones toward the side wings.
note: The Power Play opens up the centre of the ice, creating higher-scoring ends with multiple angles.

clue: An end in which neither team scores any points leaving the score unchanged.
note: In games with last-stone advantage, blanking an end allows the team to retain the hammer for the following end.

clue: Canadian curling legend who skipped her Saskatchewan rink to 1998 Olympic gold and three World Championships.
note: Affectionately nicknamed 'Schmirler the Curler,' she is celebrated as one of the greatest and most charismatic skips in history.

clue: The specialized cue used by wheelchair curlers to deliver stones from a stationary chair without sliding.
note: Wheelchair curling does not permit sweeping, making delivery stick accuracy and release weight especially critical.

clue: The time-honoured curling tradition of socializing over beverages with opponents immediately after a match.
note: Traditionally, the winning team buys the first round of drinks for their opponents, reflecting the sport's deep sportsmanship.

clue: A shot that strikes an opponent's stone to remove it and then rolls behind a guard or into the rings.
note: Executing a hit and roll accomplishes two objectives at once: eliminating a threat and securing scoring position.

clue: Scoring one or more points in an end when your team does not possess the hammer.
note: Stealing requires aggressive placement of guards and stones in the four-foot to deny the opponent an open draw.

clue: Swedish curling superstar who captured seven World Men's titles and 2022 Olympic gold as skip.
note: Edin made history by becoming the first men's skip to win four consecutive World Curling Championships from 2018 to 2022.

clue: The narrow circular ring on the bottom of a curling stone that actually makes contact with the ice.
note: The running surface is only about five millimetres wide, concentrating the stone's weight onto a tiny contact area.

clue: The wide line across the ice that stones must clearly cross to remain in play and before which the stone must be released.
note: Modern elite competitions use electronic handles with light sensors to detect whether a stone was released before the hog line.

clue: The strategic feat of holding the team holding the hammer to only a single point.
note: Forcing an opponent to take one point is generally considered a tactical defensive victory for the team without hammer.

clue: The player on a four-person team who throws the first two stones and handles primary sweeping duties.
note: Leads must possess exceptional corner-guard and draw-to-the-wings precision to set up the end's tactical layout.

clue: The annual Canadian women's curling championship whose champion wears the maple leaf at the World Championship.
note: Established under its current tournament identity in 1982, it features provincial champions and defending Team Canada.

clue: A slip-on rubber cover placed over a slider shoe to provide stable traction when walking or sweeping.
note: Curlers always remove their gripper from their sliding foot just before stepping into the hack to deliver a stone.

clue: A single powerful hit that eliminates two opposing stones from play in one shot.
note: A successful double takeout can completely neutralize an opponent's well-constructed offensive cluster in the house.

clue: The small central circle at the very core of the house surrounded by the four-foot ring.
note: Stones resting on the button are the most difficult to out-count and usually hold shot stone status.

clue: American skip who engineered a miraculous five-game winning streak to capture USA men's curling gold in 2018.
note: His team executed a stunning five-ender in the eighth end of the gold medal final against Sweden in PyeongChang.

clue: A stone in motion that is illegally touched by a player or their broom or clothing.
note: Under modern World Curling rules, the non-offending skip has options on how to handle the positions of stones after a burn.

clue: The prestigious flagship event of the Grand Slam of Curling series featuring the world's top-ranked men's and women's teams.
note: Known for having one of the deepest international fields in professional curling, it traditionally crowns the Slam season.

clue: Legendary Canadian skip nicknamed 'The Bear' who won 2010 Olympic gold and four Briers and 18 Grand Slam titles.
note: Martin was a pioneer of the aggressive corner guard strategy that revolutionized modern men's curling in the 1990s.

clue: The cumulative measurement of pre-game draws to the button used to break ties and determine hammer in playoffs.
note: Teams practice drawing to the tee with each rotation before every game, with distances measured in centimetres.

clue: The two stones pre-set on the centre line before any deliveries are made in a mixed doubles end.
note: One stone is positioned as a centre guard while the other is placed at the back of the four-foot ring.

clue: A takeout shot where a shooter strikes a guard to propel it backwards into an opponent's stone in the house.
note: Runbacks require great weight and angle precision because a slight miss will deflect the guard harmlessly away.

clue: The rubber-lined foothold anchored into the ice from which a curler pushes off to deliver a stone.
note: Two hacks are installed side by side at each end of the sheet to accommodate right-handed and left-handed throwers.

clue: The historic birthplace of curling and home to the Royal Caledonian Curling Club founded in 1838.
note: Scotland hosted the first international curling competition, the Scotch Cup, in 1959 at Falkirk and Edinburgh.

clue: The countdown clock system in elite curling that measures only the time a team spends planning and preparing shots.
note: A team's clock stops the moment the delivering player releases the stone and crosses the tee line.

clue: The team member who takes charge of house strategy while the skip is in the hack throwing stones.
note: Also known as the third, this player traditionally measures contested stones with the opponent's vice-skip.

clue: A path on the ice where stones curl abnormally hard toward one side due to a slope or depression in the sheet.
note: Ice makers continually work to ensure level sheets using computerized laser levels during mid-season maintenance.

clue: A shot where a delivered stone glances gently off the side of another stone to alter its trajectory into position.
note: Also called a carom, a successful wick can redirect a stone behind complex protective guards.

clue: An additional end played to decide the winner when a curling game is tied at the conclusion of regulation ends.
note: Ties are never permitted in competitive curling; play continues end-by-end until a champion emerges.

clue: A stone that barely overlaps the outer edge of the twelve-foot circle and remains eligible for scoring.
note: Biters are verified using a biter bar, a specialized gauge swung in a circle from the central pin.

clue: Swiss skip who led her team to an extraordinary four consecutive World Women's Curling Championship titles from 2019 to 2023.
note: Tirinzoni called team strategy while fourth thrower Alina Pätz threw the final high-pressure stones.

clue: A traditional curling tournament or festival bringing together multiple clubs and rinks for competitive and social play.
note: Bonspiels range from weekend local club socials to massive multi-sheet civic events lasting an entire week.

clue: A high-velocity takeout shot designed to remove an opponent's guard while rolling the shooter out of play as well.
note: Peeling removes clutter from the front of the sheet, keeping the house open for teams protecting a lead.

clue: Scottish skip who delivered the famous 'Stone of Destiny' to secure women's Olympic gold for Great Britain in 2002.
note: Her final draw struck the four-foot in Salt Lake City, captivating millions of late-night television viewers in the UK.

clue: A guard positioned in front of the house but away from the centre line to set up offensive play to the wings.
note: Corner guards allow teams with the hammer to build multi-point ends without clogging the middle draw path.

clue: Iconic Canadian skip who went undefeated to win Olympic gold in 2014 and collected six Scotties titles.
note: Renowned for her clutch shot-making, Jones's 'in-off' shot to win the 2005 Scotties is regarded as one of curling's greatest shots.

clue: The annual premier World Curling competition showcasing the planet's top players under twenty-one years of age.
note: Many Olympic champions, including Niklas Edin and Jennifer Jones, first proved their brilliance at World Juniors.

clue: A delivery where a right-handed thrower rotates the stone clockwise causing it to curl from right to left.
note: The opposite rotation, rotating counter-clockwise for a right-hander, is known as the out-turn.

clue: The traditional straw sweeping broom widely used before modern synthetic fabric brushes were adopted.
note: Corn brooms produced a distinctive slap against the ice to clear frost, but dropped debris that caused stones to pick.

clue: The customary act of shaking hands to end a game early when a trailing team mathematically or realistically cannot win.
note: Unlike many sports where quitting is frowned upon, curling views conceding an unwinnable match as proper respect for opponents.

clue: The line passing directly through the centre of the house perpendicular to the centre line of the sheet.
note: Once an opponent's stone crosses the tee line, the defending team is legally entitled to sweep it toward the back.

clue: A gentle hit designed to nudge an opponent's stone slightly further back into the house without completely removing it.
note: A tap back alters the relative distances from the button, promoting the shooter or an existing guard into shot stone.

clue: The Paralympic two-athlete discipline that made its world championship debut in 2022 and joined the Paralympic program.
note: Matches consist of eight ends, requiring precise stick delivery without any sweeping assistance from teammates.

clue: A tactical situation where the defending team peels all guards and removes house stones to leave an empty sheet.
note: Teams leading late in a game deliberately force clean ends to reduce the opponent's chances of constructing multi-point ends.

clue: Canadian curling pioneer who skipped his Saskatchewan family rink to four Brier and four Scotch Cup World titles from 1959 to 1963.
note: Nicknamed 'The King,' Richardson was an early global ambassador who helped popularize curling on international television.

clue: Italian curling phenom who paired with Amos Mosaner to win 2022 Olympic gold with an unblemished 11-0 record.
note: Constantini and Mosaner captured Italy's first-ever Olympic curling medal in a sensational Beijing performance.

clue: Moisture crystals that accumulate on the pebble to significantly slow stone speed and alter curl paths.
note: Frost buildup occurs when warm, humid arena air encounters cold ice surface temperatures during long sessions.

clue: A rare statistical feat where a curler completes an entire competitive match with a 100 percent shot-making rating.
note: Achieving a perfect game requires executing every designated shot, weight, and line flawlessly as graded by official scorers.

clue: The player who delivers the third and fourth stones of an end and pairs with the lead on major sweeping calls.
note: Seconds are frequently responsible for executing critical peel shots and double takeouts to manage mid-end traffic.

clue: The legendary Edmonton rink skipped by Randy Ferbey that won four Briers in five years using an innovative line-up switch.
note: Ferbey threw third stones while calling the game, while David Nedohin threw final stones under intense pressure.

clue: The sudden and unpredictable deflection of a moving stone caused by running over a hair or debris or frost clump.
note: A pick can instantly derail a well-thrown shot, making ice cleanliness a paramount concern for sweeping leads.

clue: Swedish skip who made history by holding the Olympic gold and World Championship and European Championship titles simultaneously in 2019.
note: Her rink won Olympic gold at PyeongChang 2018 and followed up with back-to-back European titles and Grand Slam crowns.

clue: The individual pre-game shots delivered by two designated players to measure proximity to the button and award first-end hammer.
note: The aggregate distances of these draws over a round robin also serve as the primary tiebreaker for championship playoff seeding.

clue: A delicate draw shot that curves around a stationary guard stone and nestles safely behind it.
note: A perfectly placed come-around makes the newly delivered stone untouchable via a direct open takeout line.

clue: The formal code of ethics enshrined in World Curling rules emphasizing mutual respect and honest calls and fair play.
note: The Spirit of Curling dictates that a true curler would rather lose than win dishonourably through an unfair advantage.

clue: The traditional embroidered crest awarded to curlers who qualify to represent their province or territory at the Brier.
note: Earning a purple heart is one of the highest badges of honour in competitive Canadian men's curling.
